sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant experimental systematic uncertainties reported by ATLAS for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios?
How do uncertainties in B-meson production fractions and fragmentation affect ATLAS branching ratio determinations?
sub_answers.text:
Uncertainties in measured branching fractions can include contributions from external measured branching ratios and unmeasured branching ratios used for normalization [d141416s0p0].
Uncertainties in the parent hadron transverse momentum spectrum affect derived branching fractions through acceptance and efficiency corrections [d141416s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What theoretical inputs (e.g., decay constants, form factors) and their uncertainties enter the interpretation of B→μμ results?
sub_answers.text:
Decay constants and transition form factors enter interpretations of B decay rates and are evaluated within quark models and lattice calculations [d10721s0p0].
Form factor numerical values and their momentum dependence carry uncertainties linked to model parameters such as wave-function beta parameters [d10721s0p0].
Electromagnetic form factors and phenomenological two-photon exchange corrections are additional theoretical inputs with associated uncertainties in related electroweak observables [d4293s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do differences among experiments or analysis methods create tensions or ambiguities in combined B→μμ constraints?
sub_answers.text:
Measured branching fractions and their agreement with Standard Model predictions can vary by multiple standard deviations depending on model assumptions used in the comparison [d125855s0p0].
Lepton-flavor-universality tests report separate statistical and systematic uncertainties that affect comparisons between muon and electron channels [d122078s0p0].
Control-sample consistency checks show residual differences at the level of fractions of a standard deviation, indicating experiment-dependent systematic and methodological variations [d141416s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What model-dependent assumptions (e.g., effective operator basis, lepton-flavor universality) lead to ambiguous theoretical interpretations?
sub_answers.text:
Analyses testing muon-electron universality explicitly assume or test lepton-flavor universality in branching-fraction ratios [d122078s0p0].
Interpretations rely on theoretical models such as covariant light-front quark models and choices of parameterizations (e.g., beta parameters) that introduce model dependence into form factors and decay-constant inputs [d10721s0p0].
Comparisons to Standard Model predictions depend on specific model assumptions, leading to consistency levels that vary with those assumptions [d125855s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
sub_answers.text: Scalar and vector leptoquark models are constrained by ATLAS measurements related to b→sμ+μ− observables and dedicated leptoquark searches [d71088s0p0][d69058s0p0]. Z′ models addressing b→sℓ+ℓ− transitions are constrained by LHC di-muon resonance searches and penguin-type explanations of b→sℓ+ℓ− data [d37511s0p0]. Models with vector-like fermions that modify flavor observables are constrained through combined fits to b→sℓℓ branching ratios and angular observables [d72444s0p0][d60942s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
What branching ratio for B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS collaboration report and in which publication/year?
What branching ratio or upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS report and in which dataset or year?
What are the statistical and systematic uncertainties quoted by ATLAS for these branching ratio measurements?
Which datasets (integrated luminosity, collision energy) and triggers did ATLAS use for the rare B→μμ analyses?
What significance or confidence level did ATLAS report for the observation or exclusion of B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− decays?
What muon identification and reconstruction algorithms does ATLAS employ for low-rate B→μμ decays?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS uses upgraded high-precision muon tracking detectors to increase the acceptance for precision muon momentum measurement and triggering in low-rate analyses [d36328s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What event selection criteria and multivariate classifiers did ATLAS use to separate signal from background in B→μμ searches?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS selects opposite-sign muon pairs and categorizes events with and without b-tagged jets for dimuon searches [d48617s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does ATLAS model and estimate combinatorial and peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− analyses?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS characterizes long-range and high-angle muon backgrounds by benchmarking Monte Carlo simulations against experimental muon flux measurements to identify sources such as diffractive proton losses and to enable mitigation strategies [d121223s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What fitting procedures and likelihood functions does ATLAS use to extract yields and branching fractions for B→μμ?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS extracts signal strengths and cross-section limits using profile likelihood fits in analyses of processes with similar final states [d98527s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are detector acceptance, efficiency, and trigger corrections determined and validated in ATLAS B→μμ measurements?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS validates detector acceptance and efficiency models by benchmarking Monte Carlo muon flux simulations against experimental measurements, achieving agreement within 10–15% across configurations [d121223s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which experimental systematic errors dominate ATLAS’s uncertainty budget for the measured branching fractions of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− (for example muon ID/reconstruction, trigger efficiency, mass resolution, background modelling), and what are their numerical contributions?

In ATLAS’s published analyses, how are the uncertainties on B-meson production fractions (f_s, f_d) and on b-quark fragmentation functions propagated into the extracted B→μμ branching ratios, and what fractional shift or uncertainty do they induce?
sub_answers.text:
Uncertainties on the probabilities for b quarks to hadronize into B_s^0 and B^0 mesons are included in branching-fraction systematics via the normalization procedure using measured production fractions and hadronization ratios [d34883s0p0].
The model dependence associated with time-dependent efficiency and the B_s lifetime difference can produce an effect close to 10% on B_s branching-fraction determinations and thus implicitly affects the propagated uncertainty from production/fragmentation inputs [d43378s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What external theoretical inputs (for instance lattice-QCD decay constants f_Bs and f_Bd, CKM matrix elements, short-distance Wilson coefficients, and electroweak/radiative corrections) are used to convert measured signal yields into branching ratios for B_s^0 and B^0 → μ^+μ^−, and what are the quoted uncertainties on each of those inputs?
sub_answers.text: Conversion of measured yields into B_s^0 branching fractions is sensitive to the treatment of the B_s mass-eigenstate lifetime difference and the time dependence of the experimental efficiency, which introduces an approximate 10% numerical impact in realistic cases where new physics is a correction to SM dynamics [d43378s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: When comparing ATLAS results to those from CMS, LHCb, or previous combinations, which methodological or calibration differences (e.g., normalization channels, fit models, treatment of peaking backgrounds, lifetime acceptance corrections) produce the largest discrepancies or contribute most to the combined fit tensions for B→μμ measurements?
sub_answers.text:
Differences in the treatment of lifetime acceptance corrections and the time-dependent efficiency for B_s mesons affect comparisons and combinations between experiments and can lead to methodological tensions in branching-fraction results [d43378s0p0].
Differences in muon-system performance, including momentum resolution and spatial resolution of the muon spectrometer, are relevant experimental calibration differences between experiments and detectors used in B→μμ measurements [d12480s0p0][d43425s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which theoretical/phenomenological assumptions (such as the chosen effective Hamiltonian/operator basis, assumptions about lepton-flavour universality, inclusion or omission of scalar/pseudoscalar operators, or SM-like lifetime/CPV properties) can change the interpretation of the measured B_s^0 and B^0 → μ^+μ^− rates, and how do these assumptions quantitatively alter inferred constraints on new-physics Wilson coefficients?
sub_answers.text:
Assuming SM-like lifetime and CP properties for the B_s system versus allowing non-SM lifetime or CP-violating effects changes the interpretation of measured rates and can shift inferred constraints on new-physics contributions by an amount that can be close to 10% in representative scenarios [d43378s0p0].
Tests of lepton-flavour universality and choices about which operator basis or whether to include scalar/pseudoscalar operators alter the phenomenological interpretation of measured branching fractions and the mapping to Wilson coefficients, as illustrated by precision LFU studies in related B→K*ℓℓ modes [d122078s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS searches for lepton-flavour-violating and lepton-flavour-universality observables provide direct experimental input used to test and constrain models proposed to explain b→sℓℓ anomalies and LFUV measurements such as R(K) and R(J/ψ) [d96369s0p0].
Model-parameter spaces are constrained by ATLAS data in global interpretations, and model-building studies report limits on parameter combinations from collider and flavour observables when fitting to data [d60942s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
sub_answers.text:
Scalar and vector leptoquark scenarios addressing b→sμ+μ− anomalies are constrained by ATLAS searches and measurements related to muon-flavour signatures [d71088s0p0].
Models featuring vector-like fermions and extensions linking to the flavor sector are constrained by ATLAS data through limits on production, decay, and fermion mixing parameters [d60942s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
Provide the branching fraction value ATLAS published for the decay B_s^0 → μ^+μ^−, specifying the exact paper title, journal reference (or arXiv ID) and publication year in which that result appears.

Give ATLAS's reported central value or 95% (or 90%) CL upper limit for the decay B^0 → μ^+μ^−, and state which dataset (year(s) of data-taking or run period) and paper or conference note this result was derived from.

List the numerical statistical and systematic uncertainties ATLAS quoted for the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− branching measurements (e.g., ±stat, ±syst), indicating which uncertainty corresponds to which decay and where in the publication these numbers appear (table or equation reference).

Specify the ATLAS datasets used for the rare B→μ^+μ^− analyses: give integrated luminosity (in fb^−1) and centre-of-mass energy (e.g., 7, 8, 13 TeV) for each data-taking period, and name the trigger selections or trigger paths used to collect the signal candidates as reported by ATLAS.

State the statistical significance or confidence intervals ATLAS reported for observing or excluding B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− (e.g., local significance in σ, p-value, or reported CLs limits), and cite where in the ATLAS result these significance/CL values are given.

Which specific muon reconstruction and identification strategies does ATLAS use in low-rate B_s0/B0→μ+μ− searches (e.g., combined, segment-tagged, calorimeter-tagged, standalone muons), and which algorithm versions, track-fitting approaches, and quality/compatibility criteria are applied to maximize efficiency while suppressing punch-through and cosmic-ray backgrounds?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS employs precision muon tracking with Muon Drift Tube (MDT) chambers and upgraded small-diameter MDT (sMDT) chambers to increase acceptance for precision muon momentum measurement and improve rate capability in high-background regions [d36328s0p0]. The first-level muon trigger decision can incorporate MDT chamber data using a fast MDT read-out chain and a fast MDT track reconstruction algorithm to reduce low-momentum-trigger dominated rates [d32191s0p0]. The inner ATLAS silicon pixel detector provides high-resolution tracking that refines charged-track pattern recognition and resolves primary and secondary vertices for flavor tagging and vertexing of B-decays [d6341s0p0]. Upgrades and demonstrators for fast MDT readout and fast reconstruction have been tested for low-latency operation to enable selective muon triggering under high-luminosity conditions [d32191s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What exact event preselection cuts and multivariate discriminants were implemented by ATLAS to separate B_s0/B0→μ+μ− signal from backgrounds — for instance, the numerical pT and η thresholds, vertex χ2 and pointing-angle requirements, isolation definitions, BDT/BDTG or neural-network architectures, training samples and input variable lists, and any category-specific or trigger-dependent selection schemes?

How does ATLAS quantify and model the combinatorial background versus peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0→μ+μ− analyses — specifically, what sideband interpolation methods, control samples (e.g., like-sign, mass-sidebands, B+→J/ψK+, Drell–Yan), misidentification rates for hadrons faking muons, and dedicated simulated or data-driven templates are used to estimate each background component and associated uncertainties?

What exact likelihood or fitting framework does ATLAS employ to extract signal yields and translate them to branching fractions in B_s0/B0→μ+μ− searches — for example, whether they use unbinned extended maximum-likelihood fits, simultaneous fits to mass and multivariate output or to multiple categories, the parameterisation of signal mass shapes (Crystal Ball, double Gaussian), background models, treatment of nuisance parameters and constraints, and procedure for obtaining confidence intervals or upper limits (profile likelihood, Feldman–Cousins, CLs)?

How are acceptance, reconstruction and trigger efficiencies evaluated and cross-checked in ATLAS B_s0/B0→μ+μ− measurements — including which MC generators and detector simulation (GEANT4) versions are used, how tag-and-probe on J/ψ→μ+μ− or Z→μ+μ− is used to derive data/MC scale factors, the methods for applying kinematic- and category-dependent corrections, and what closure tests or control-channel comparisons validate the efficiency and systematic uncertainty assignments?

Which detector-related and analysis-driven systematic uncertainties (trigger/reconstruction efficiencies, muon ID, mass resolution, background modeling, luminosity) dominate ATLAS's reported error budget for the B_s0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fraction measurements, and what are their quoted magnitudes?

Quantify how uncertainties in the b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d), fragmentation functions, and b-quark cross-section used by ATLAS propagate into the extracted B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios; which of these production/fragmentation inputs is the largest contributor?

List the external theoretical inputs ATLAS uses to convert signal yields into branching ratios (e.g., decay constants f_Bs, f_B, CKM elements, lifetime corrections, form factors) and give the stated uncertainties or sources (lattice QCD, sum rules) for each that enter the B→μ+μ interpretation.

Identify specific analysis choices or methodological differences (normalization channels, background subtraction techniques, event selection, fit models, treatment of peaking backgrounds) between ATLAS and other experiments (CMS, LHCb) that lead to inconsistent central values or uncertainties in combined B→μ+μ results.

Specify the model-dependent theoretical assumptions that affect the mapping from measured branching ratios to new-physics constraints (choice of effective operators, assumed lepton-flavor universality, right-handed currents, use of SM effective lifetime vs. time-integrated rates), and explain which assumptions produce the largest ambiguity in interpreting deviations.

Which Wilson coefficients (C7, C9, C10 and their primed, scalar and pseudoscalar counterparts) are most tightly limited by the ATLAS measurement of the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− branching ratio, and what numerical bounds or confidence intervals do ATLAS results imply for those coefficients within the weak effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ?

In combined global fits of b→sℓℓ observables that test lepton-flavor universality and non‑SM scalar/pseudoscalar operators, how does inclusion of ATLAS B_s^0→μ^+μ^− data shift the best-fit values, uncertainties, or pull of scenarios (e.g., C9μ vs. C9e, C10 vs. C10′, CS, CP) compared with fits excluding ATLAS?

For concrete new-physics frameworks — for example MSSM variants with large tanβ, simplified Z′ boson models with flavor-changing b–s couplings, and specific leptoquark representations (scalar S_3, vector U_1) — what regions of parameter space (coupling strengths, masses, tanβ) are excluded or disfavored by the ATLAS B_s^0→μ^+μ^− branching-fraction measurement?

By what procedure do groups that produce world averages (such as the Heavy Flavor Averaging Group or the PDG) include ATLAS upper limits and central-value measurements for B_s^0→μ^+μ^− when constructing combined branching-ratio constraints, and how are correlated systematic uncertainties and differing confidence-level conventions from ATLAS handled in those averages used for model-exclusion studies?

Based on ATLAS upgrade projections (HL-LHC luminosity, improved muon triggers and vertexing), what quantitative improvements in the B_s^0→μ^+μ^− branching-ratio precision or upper-limit reach are expected, and how would those improvements translate into stronger bounds on specific flavor-violating Wilson coefficients or on new-physics coupling×(1/mass^2) combinations?

Provide the value ATLAS published for the branching fraction of Bs0 → μ+μ−, and cite the specific paper or conference note and its publication year (include journal reference or arXiv ID if available).

Give the branching fraction measurement or the upper limit reported by ATLAS for B0 → μ+μ−, specifying which dataset/year or analysis version that result comes from (e.g., Run 1, Run 2, specific integrated luminosity or year).

List the numerical statistical and systematic error components ATLAS quoted for the Bs0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching-ratio results (separate values for statistical and systematic uncertainties and indicate which applies to which decay).

Specify the ATLAS datasets used in the muon-pair rare-B analyses: give the integrated luminosity values, the proton–proton collision center-of-mass energies (e.g., 7, 8, 13 TeV), the data-taking years, and the primary trigger selections or muon triggers employed in the analysis.

State the significance levels, p-values, or confidence intervals ATLAS reported for observing or excluding the Bs0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− decays (e.g., number of standard deviations, 95% CL upper limits), and indicate which number corresponds to which decay channel.

Which specific muon reconstruction chains, identification criteria (e.g., combined, segment-tagged, standalone), and low-momentum reconstruction strategies has ATLAS deployed when searching for rare B→μμ decays, and how do these differ from standard high-rate muon workflows?
sub_answers.text: ATLAS measures muons with a muon spectrometer composed of precision tracking and trigger chambers embedded in a 2 T toroidal magnetic field for momentum measurement [d12480s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What precise event preselection cuts, kinematic and topological variables, and machine-learning classifiers (for example BDT or neural-net architectures and input feature sets) has ATLAS trained and applied to discriminate B→μμ signal candidates from continuum and heavy-flavor background?

By what data-driven techniques and simulation studies does ATLAS quantify and separate combinatorial background versus peaking backgrounds (such as B→hh with misidentified hadrons, semileptonic decays, or cascade decays) in Bs0 and B0 → μ+μ− searches, including control samples and mis-ID rate measurements used?

Describe the statistical models ATLAS fits to the dimuon mass (and auxiliary) distributions: which extended unbinned/binned likelihoods, component PDFs (signal shapes, resolution models, background parameterizations), nuisance parameters, and fit validation tests are used to extract signal yields and convert them into branching ratios?

How does ATLAS determine and validate the total acceptance and efficiency corrections for B→μμ measurements—covering trigger, reconstruction, and selection efficiencies—including use of Monte Carlo, tag-and-probe studies in J/ψ→μμ or other control channels, data/MC scale factors, and systematic uncertainty evaluation?
sub_answers.text: The ATLAS pixel detector provides high-acceptance, high-resolution tracking that largely defines the ability to resolve primary and secondary vertices used in heavy-flavor and rare-decay analyses [d6341s0p0].
